We need to determine whether "Gary is blue" follows from facts and rules. We have facts: Erin is big, blue, kind, not nice, not round. Gary is not round, white. Also we have rules:

1. If someone is kind and cold then they are not blue.
2. Nice people are big.
3. All round people are big.
4. If someone is white then they are big.
5. If someone is white and blue then they are not round.
6. Big people are kind.
7. If someone is nice and cold then they are kind.
8. If someone is white then they are cold.

We need to see if we can deduce Gary is blue. We have Gary is white (fact). From rule 8: If someone is white then they are cold. So Gary is cold. Also from rule 4: If someone is white then they are big. So Gary is big. Also rule 6: Big people are kind. So Gary is kind. Also rule 2: Nice people are big (but we don't have nice). Rule 3: All round people are big (not relevant). Rule 1: If someone is kind and cold then they are not blue. We have Gary is kind and cold, so we can infer: Gary is not blue. So we get Gary is not blue. Thus the statement "Gary is blue" is false; we can deduce its negation.

Thus answer is False.
